Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'uncommon' (potions.py:930), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:920-937)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

ExtraHoverTips.maps_to: no counterpart; the sim has no hover-tip surface
ExtraHoverTips.rationale: ExtraHoverTips / HoverTipFactory / PotionModel.HoverTip are the potion tooltip's keyword lines. Waived under the shared contract's presentation exclusion, not under any unreachability claim.

OnUse (protected override, Ashwater.cs:2.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4, NARROWED 2026-07-27. The verbs, the count and the hook order all matched already. Of the MinSelect-0 divergence only one thing remains: neither call site passes the `min_select` parameter CombatState.select_cards now has (combat.py:665-705), so the selectorless engine default still takes every candidate. With the env's scripted selector (selectors.py:83-89, installed at full_env.py:788) the partial pick is now expressed correctly and the screen's 'confirm none' outcome is reachable. See guard G1 for the executed witnesses.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): MinSelect 0 -- the game lets you exhaust ANY NUMBER of cards including none; the sim always exhausts every candidate
guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27: partly closed. CombatState.select_cards now carries the missing pair -- `min_select: int | None = None` (combat.py:665-705), read at combat.py:693 into `floor`, with combat.py:699-702 letting the selectorless path return anywhere from `floor` to `count`, none included. The two MinSelect-0 potions also stopped sharing the fixed-count 'exhaust' purpose: they now ask for the dedicated `exhaust_any` / `discard_any` labels, and selectors.py:83-89 answers those by FILTERING the candidates to Statuses/Curses instead of taking `count` of them -- and scripted_card_selector is what the env installs by default (full_env.py:788). EXECUTED (2026-07-27) with that selector, hand [strike, defend, bash, wound]: Ashwater exhausts only the wound. WHAT REMAINS: no call site anywhere passes `min_select`. An executed `grep -rn min_select sts2_rl/` returns only the parameter, its docstring and the `floor` line in combat.py, so both potions still call select_cards with min_select=None, `floor` collapses to `count`, and the SELECTORLESS engine default (CombatState's own default, and full_env.py:788's documented `card_selector=None` option) still takes every candidate. EXECUTED at seeds 0-3: Ashwater's hand 4 -> 0 with a 4-card exhaust pile; Gambler's Brew discards all 3. Downgraded from LIVE to dormant -- no production path is selectorless (the env installs the scripted selector, the conformance driver installs the recorded picks) -- but the fix is one keyword argument at each of the two call sites. Shared with the sibling MinSelect-0 potion; one mechanism, two sites.

guards.what: N1: the exhaust verb itself -- `CardCmd.Exhaust(choiceContext, item)` (Ashwater.cs:32) vs ExhaustCmd.exhaust (cmds.py:371-384)
guards.rationale: The sim removes the card from whichever of hand/discard holds it, appends it to the exhaust pile and fires on_card_exhausted (cmds.py:379-384), and the loop order is the selection order on both sides. Exhaust's own hook surface belongs to audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json and is not re-verdicted here.

guards.what: N2: `CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding -> return Array.Empty` (CardSelectCmd.cs:694-697) has no sim counterpart in select_cards
guards.rationale: Structurally satisfied rather than dropped: CombatState.use_potion refuses to run at all unless `self.phase == Phase.PLAYER_TURN` (combat.py:591-592), and _end_combat sets the phase to COMBAT_OVER, so a potion cannot open a selection screen during a combat that is over or ending. Checked deliberately because it is the guard a mid-effect kill would trip, and Ashwater cannot kill.

guards.what: N3: Ashwater has no numeric constant and no ascension branch
guards.rationale: Ashwater.cs is 35 lines and declares no CanonicalVars block; the only literals are the tint colour and the 0/999999999 selector bounds, which G1 covers. `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-vars` reports C#=[] sim={} for this unit, so PROMPT.md bug classes 19 (a docstring misquoting a constant) and the GetValueIfAscension argument-order trap have nothing to bite.
